success-green.purpose: Identity fill for confirmation surfaces and on-target planner days; pair with success-ink for text.

success-ink.purpose: Text-safe green (4.8:1 on Paper White) for confirmation copy.

warning-amber.purpose: Identity fill for attention surfaces, AI-estimate dots and over-target planner days; pair with warning-ink for text.

warning-ink.purpose: Text-safe amber (4.7:1 on Paper White) for warning copy, estimate badges and provenance markers.

title.purpose: Screen/sub-screen name in the sticky header — the only heading-weight text in the app. Its 28px line-height matches the back button's 36px tap target.

body.purpose: Default control and copy size on desktop.

body-mobile-input.purpose: Text/decimal inputs on mobile; 16px is load-bearing against iOS Safari zoom-on-focus.

label.purpose: Field labels, hints, error text, nav labels, macro captions.

micro.purpose: Floor of the type scale, one size (11px): uppercase tracking-wider eyebrows and sparing sentence-case captions, reused across ~15 files.

shadows.name: header-lift
shadows.purpose: Sticky AppHeader separating pinned chrome from scrolled content.

shadows.name: popover-lift
shadows.purpose: Transient content anchored to a point rather than the layout — the weight chart's value tooltip.

shadows.name: overlay-lift
shadows.purpose: BottomSheet and the centered confirm dialog — content that covers the page.

shadows.name: photo-scrim
shadows.purpose: Not a shadow: the translucent black plate that keeps a control legible over user photography. Hover raises it to 0.75.

motion.name: color-transition
motion.purpose: Default hover/focus state change on buttons, inputs and nav items.

motion.name: sheet-height
motion.purpose: BottomSheet height transitions between fixed and content-sized.

motion.name: skeleton-pulse
motion.purpose: Soft Lavender placeholder blocks standing in for list rows and form fields while data loads.

motion.name: action-spinner
motion.purpose: 16px lucide Loader2 inside the button that started long-running work (AI photo import), next to a label naming the wait.

motion.name: bar-fill
motion.purpose: Macro goal bar widths slide to a new value instead of jumping.

motion.name: reduced-motion-guard
motion.purpose: Global collapse of every animation and transition — motion is never the sole carrier of meaning.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single primary action of a screen or sheet.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: hsl(244 36% 44%); color: hsl(0 0% 100%); padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border-radius: 6px; border: none; transition: background-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: hsl(244 36% 44% / 0.9); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid hsl(249 72% 65%); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action next to a primary one (cancel, alternative path).
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: hsl(300 100% 99%); color: hsl(0 0% 20%); padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid hsl(240 9% 78%); transition: background-color 150ms; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: hsl(240 33% 94%); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid hsl(249 72% 65%); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Icon Button
components.description: Button variant=quiet|quietDestructive|onDark|scrim with size=icon (40px) or iconSm (36px). The scrim variant shown here is the photo-overlay case; quiet/quietDestructive are the same box with a transparent rest state. The accent variant (bg accent/10, indigo glyph) is the repeating add-to-slot affordance on the diary and planner.
components.css: .ds-btn-icon { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; width: 36px; flex-shrink: 0; border: none; border-radius: 6px; background: transparent; transition: background-color 150ms, color 150ms; } .ds-btn-icon:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid hsl(249 72% 65%); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-btn-icon:disabled { opacity: 0.5; pointer-events: none; } .ds-btn-icon--quiet { color: hsl(0 0% 36%); } .ds-btn-icon--quiet:hover { background: hsl(240 33% 94%); color: hsl(0 0% 20%); } .ds-btn-icon--destructive { color: hsl(0 0% 36%); } .ds-btn-icon--destructive:hover { background: hsl(0 84% 60% / 0.1); color: hsl(0 84% 60%); } .ds-btn-icon--scrim { height: 40px; width: 40px; background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.6); color: #fff; backdrop-filter: blur(2px); } .ds-btn-icon--scrim:hover { background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.75); } .ds-btn-icon--accent { height: 40px; width: 40px; background: hsl(249 72% 65% / 0.1); color: hsl(244 36% 44%); } .ds-btn-icon--accent:hover { background: hsl(249 72% 65% / 0.2); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: The app's text/decimal input. text-base on mobile is load-bearing against iOS Safari zoom-on-focus.
components.css: .ds-input { background: hsl(300 100% 99%); color: hsl(0 0% 20%); border: 1px solid hsl(240 9% 78%); border-radius: 6px; padding: 8px 12px; font-size: 0.875rem; min-width: 0; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid hsl(249 72% 65%); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The app's surface primitive — flat, bordered, no shadow.
components.css: .ds-card { background: hsl(240 100% 98%); border: 1px solid hsl(240 9% 78%); border-radius: 8px; padding: 16px; }

components.name: Status Banner
components.description: One primitive for all three tones (error/warning/success) in two densities. Names what happened, what to do about it, and carries its own recovery control.
components.html:
Aus diesen Fotos ließ sich kein Rezept lesen.

Achte auf scharfen, vollständig sichtbaren Text und versuche es erneut.
components.css: .ds-banner { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; border-radius: 6px; padding: 12px; font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-banner--error { border: 1px solid hsl(0 84% 60% / 0.5); background: hsl(0 84% 60% / 0.1); color: hsl(0 84% 60%); } .ds-banner--warning { border: 1px solid hsl(38 92% 50% / 0.5); background: hsl(38 92% 50% / 0.05); color: hsl(0 0% 20%); } .ds-banner--success { border: 1px solid hsl(160 84% 39% / 0.5); background: hsl(160 84% 39% / 0.1); color: hsl(160 84% 39%); } .ds-banner-title { margin: 0; font-weight: 500; } .ds-banner-hint { margin: 0; font-size: 0.75rem; } .ds-banner-action { align-self: flex-start; background: hsl(300 100% 99%); color: hsl(0 0% 20%); border: 1px solid hsl(240 9% 78%); border-radius: 6px; padding: 4px 12px; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; } .ds-banner-action:hover { background: hsl(240 33% 94%); }

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: Signature component: picks exactly one of a handful of mutually exclusive, always-visible options via hidden native radios.
components.css: .ds-segmented { display: flex; gap: 8px; } .ds-segmented-option { flex: 1; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid hsl(240 9% 78%); padding: 8px 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 0.875rem; cursor: pointer; } .ds-segmented-option--selected { border-color: hsl(244 36% 44%); background: hsl(244 36% 44% / 0.1); font-weight: 500; }

components.name: Bottom Sheet
components.description: Signature component: portal-rendered drawer used for every full-screen form/picker/search flow instead of a route change.
components.html: Sheet content
components.css: .ds-sheet-backdrop { position: fixed; inset: 0; background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.4); } .ds-sheet { position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0; background: hsl(300 100% 99%); box-shadow: 0 10px 15px -3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 4px 6px -4px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); height: 82dvh; transition: height 200ms; } .ds-sheet-handle { margin: 8px auto 0; height: 4px; width: 40px; flex-shrink: 0; border-radius: 9999px; background: hsl(240 33% 94%); }

components.name: App Header
components.description: Signature component: sticky indigo-gradient header naming the current screen, with optional macro-goal cells.
components.css: .ds-header { position: sticky; top: 0; background-image: linear-gradient(160deg, hsl(244 36% 47%), hsl(244 38% 40%)); border-bottom: 1px solid rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); padding: 12px 16px; color: white; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); } .ds-header-title { font-size: 1.125rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.75rem; }

components.name: Select
components.description: Native select on the Input base — the platform picker beats a custom listbox on a phone. Wires itself to a surrounding Field and forwards a ref for form libraries.
components.css: .ds-select { width: 100%; background: hsl(300 100% 99%); color: hsl(0 0% 20%); border: 1px solid hsl(240 9% 78%); border-radius: 6px; padding: 8px 12px; font-size: 0.875rem; min-width: 0; } .ds-select:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid hsl(249 72% 65%); outline-offset: 1px; }

narrative.overview:
forkcast treats meal planning and fitness/weight goals as one discipline, not two apps stitched together: the same screen that plans Tuesday's dinner also reads against the macro goal driving it. The visual language matches that — a precision instrument built for someone with a full-time job and a young family, meant to be operated correctly in seconds, not admired. Training Indigo is the single signature note (primary actions, the sticky header gradient); everything else stays quiet — flat lavender-tinted neutrals, thin borders, no decorative texture — so the indigo and the three fixed macro-identity colors (protein green, carb amber, fat blue) are the only things that ever call for attention.

Density is deliberately high but never cramped: dense rows (ingredient amounts, log entries) use the sm control size and tabular numerals so figures line up; primary screens use the roomier md size that clears a comfortable tap target. The system has no ornamental flourish, no illustration, no imagery — it is entirely typographic, icon-coded and color-coded, and German-only (lang="de", no i18n abstraction beyond the single locale). Icons come from one library (lucide-react, ~19 files) at a consistent stroke; a Unicode glyph is never an icon.

Motion exists but is strictly informational, never decorative: a pulse on skeleton placeholders while data loads, a spinner on an action that takes longer than a moment, a 200ms height transition on the bottom sheet, and a width transition on macro goal bars. Nothing enters, slides, fades in or parallaxes. A global prefers-reduced-motion rule collapses every animation and transition to 0.01ms, so any motion added to this system must remain optional to comprehension.
keyCharacteristics: One accent color (Training Indigo) for commitment/primary action; a brighter sibling (Bright Periwinkle) for focus and interactive accents only
Flat-at-rest, bordered surfaces; shadow reserved for things floating above the page
Fixed three-color macro identity system (protein/carb/fat) that never changes meaning
System font stack only — no custom typeface, no display type
Tight, native-app-like density with iOS-safe input sizing (16px minimum on mobile)
One drawn icon set (lucide) and informational-only motion, both held to a fixed vocabulary

rules.name: The One Indigo Rule
rules.body: Training Indigo fills at most one control per screen — the single primary action or the header. Every other button variant (outline, ghost, destructiveOutline) stays neutral or uses indigo as text only, never as a second fill competing with the primary action.

rules.name: The Macro Identity Rule
rules.body: Protein/carb/fat always render in their fixed green/amber/blue identity color for the dot and bar. Only the accompanying value text may re-tint for status (over/under goal); the identity color itself never changes meaning or gets reused for anything else.

rules.name: The Status-Token Rule
rules.body: Success, warning and error states are built from the success / warning / destructive tokens, never from a raw palette utility (amber-50, emerald-600, red-100). Audit test: a status surface whose class list contains a numbered Tailwind color is a bug, not a variant. Carb Amber and Warning Amber are different colors with different jobs — a warning never borrows the macro token, and a macro never borrows the status token.

rules.name: The Fill-Is-Not-Ink Rule
rules.body: bg-success / bg-warning paint dots, bars and tinted surfaces; status text uses text-success-ink / text-warning-ink. Audit test: text-success or text-warning on a light background is a contrast bug (~2.5:1) — the ink variants exist for exactly that position.

rules.name: The No-Display-Type Rule
rules.body: There is no hero/display type scale. The 18px header title is the ceiling; introducing anything larger breaks the instrument-not-billboard character.

rules.name: The Micro-Is-The-Floor Rule
rules.body: 11px is the smallest text the system uses — one size, not a shrinking ramp. Below Label, text is either an uppercase tracking-wider eyebrow or a sparing one-line caption; it is never a shrunk paragraph.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat and bordered at rest. Shadow is reserved for things that are literally floating above the page (sticky header, popover, sheet, dialog) — never used to add weight to an ordinary card or button. A selected state is a fill and weight change, never a lift: the white-pill-with-shadow segmented control is a borrowed iOS idiom, not this system's. Audit test: if the element scrolls with the page, it has no shadow.

rules.name: The Scrim-Over-Photo Rule
rules.body: A control placed over user photography earns contrast from a translucent black scrim and white glyph, never from a shadow or a light chip. Photo content is unpredictable; the scrim is the only treatment guaranteed to stay legible.

rules.name: The Two-Radius Rule
rules.body: Interactive controls you act on directly — buttons, inputs, segmented-control options, icon buttons — use md (6px). Containers that hold content — cards, list shells, media frames, the icon plate that fronts a list row — use lg (8px). Overlays that float above the page use xl (12px): the bottom sheet on its leading edge, a centered confirm dialog on all four corners. Micro-elements below control size — badges, source chips, skeleton bars, native checkboxes — use sm (4px). Bare `rounded` is not part of the scale. Audit test: a rounded-xl outside an overlay, a rounded-lg on something you click, or a bare rounded anywhere is a bug.

rules.name: The Pill-Means-Not-A-Box Rule
rules.body: rounded-full marks an element that is a token, a dot or a track — a chip, a status dot, a progress bar, a drag handle. A rectangular control (button, input, card) never becomes a pill.

dos: Do keep Training Indigo to one fill per screen (the primary action or the header) — see The One Indigo Rule.
Do use the fixed macro green/amber/blue for protein/carb/fat identity everywhere they appear, never reassigned.
Do build every status surface from the success / warning / destructive tokens at low opacity with a matching border, and set status text in the -ink sibling.
Do use text-base (16px) for any text input rendered on mobile — smaller sizes trigger iOS Safari's zoom-on-focus.
Do route full-screen forms/pickers through BottomSheet rather than a new route, keeping the header/nav context in place.
Do keep numeric values tabular (tabular-nums) wherever a figure updates or several must align in a column.
Do draw icons from lucide-react, mark them aria-hidden, and label the control that holds them.
Do give a control over a photo a 40px target and a black scrim; give overlay chrome 44px.
Do pair an error message with what to do next, and put the recovery control inside the banner.
Do pick the radius from what the element is — control md, container lg, overlay xl, micro-element sm — and never write bare rounded.

Do reach for the primitive before the class string: Button (with quiet / quietDestructive / onDark / scrim / accent and icon / iconSm), Banner, Select, Input, Field, Card, SegmentedControl. If none fits, add a variant there rather than a one-off at the call site.
donts: Don't add a shadow to an element that isn't literally floating above the page (ordinary cards and buttons stay flat with a border).
Don't introduce a display/hero type size — 18px semibold is the ceiling.
Don't fill a second control with Training Indigo on the same screen as the primary action; use outline or ghost instead.
Don't reuse a macro-identity color (protein/carb/fat) for anything other than that macro.
Don't reach for a numbered Tailwind color (amber-50, emerald-600) for a status surface — the tokens exist, and the app has no remaining call site that does this.
Don't set status text in the saturated fill token (text-success, text-warning); that pairing fails contrast on every light surface in the app.

Don't stand a Unicode glyph in for an icon — no ✕, ↑, ‹, → anywhere in a control. The app is glyph-free as of this revision; the only remaining Unicode operator is the × between a piece count and its per-piece weight, which is arithmetic, not an icon.
Don't add motion outside the sanctioned vocabulary (skeleton pulse, action spinner, sheet height, bar fill) — no entrances, slides, fades or parallax.
Don't show a raw server or fetch message to the user; map it to a German sentence that names the problem and the recovery.

Don't hand-roll an icon button (inline-flex h-9 w-9 items-center justify-center …) or a status surface (rounded-md border border-warning/50 bg-warning/10 p-3 …) — both are primitives now, and hand-rolled copies are how the 36/40/44px sizes drifted apart in the first place.
